key_insight: A machine-learned interatomic potential enables cation-arrangement screening in (MoWNbTaV)S₂, revealing that vibrational entropy changes stability rankings and vibrational spectra provide identification fingerprints.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports temperature-aware screening and experimental characterisation of two-dimensional high-entropy materials beyond the sampling reach of DFT alone.
method: Train a Gaussian approximation potential on DFT data through iterative learning.
Calculate Gibbs free energies and test thermal stability with nanosecond molecular dynamics.
Analyse Raman and infrared spectra for configuration-sensitive fingerprints.
evidence_signal: Five selected configurations retained their trigonal-prismatic framework during nanosecond molecular dynamics up to 1300 K, while calculated spectra combined parent-monolayer signatures with disorder-activated modes.
watch_item: Stability of five configurations over nanosecond timescales does not establish which cation arrangement forms under experimental synthesis conditions.
paper_title: Prediction and characterisation of cation topology of pentanary high-entropy alloy (MoWNbTaV)S$_2$
